Every upcoming task, everything that has caused anxiety or similar, and then I prioritize them in an agenda. dialog.text: Family is a great support, then you will definitely grow and you don't have to take any stress because you have everything there with you.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Do you have dependents that look up to you?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes, I have kids. To look them up I need to stay motivated and positive because I am the reflection to them.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: that is trueI feel relieved chating with youThank you for your words of encouragements. It really helped a lot
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That's my pleasure that my words helped you. Stay happy calm and motivated and rest you have big support of your family.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Enjoy the rest of your day.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You too! byee
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: bye.
dialog.speaker: seeker

situation: I am having a hard time at work, my workload is too big and it's making me very stressed and anxious. I can't keep up with the amount of work I'm being asked to do.

dialog.text: Hi, how are you today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Not doing so well today, I'm having a really hard time at work. I'm feeling super stressed about the workload I have, I just can't keep up with it all!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I’m sorry to hear that. Work can be a bad source of stress. Do you have anyone that can help with the workload?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Not really, there's only me in my role so don't really have anyone to help. I have tried talking to my line manager but she doesn't seem to understand just how busy I am.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Can the company hire any more people? Maybe they can work from home, and take some work off your plate. The line manager might also need some help with her workload.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I understand that budgets can be tight. Maybe someone part-time?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: From what I hear they aren't willing to hire anyone else, but I don't know the reasons why. I can only speak to my line manager and then she speaks to higher management.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Your manager sounds unsympathetic. That's very frustrating. A lot of people are in your situation in this pandemic: too much work, not enough help.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Do you want to leave the company? Look for greener pastures?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have been keeping an eye out for other jobs, but like you say things are difficult just now with the pandemic, there isn't a lot out there!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Very true. Have you talked to your co-workers about this issue? What do they think?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: They are all feeling stretched as well so they understand. I am trying to not talk about it too much with them, I don't want to be seen as the person who's always complaining!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yeah, that's a good point. A little complaining is ok, but a lot can get on people's nerves.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: They want to be sympathetic, but after a while, they just get tired of you.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yeah, I don't want them all to stop talking to me cause they find me annoying! I'm trying to stay positive, but it's hard some days! As much as I try to start the day in a positive frame of mind it quickly gets sucked out of me!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: What do you do outside of work? Hobbies and such.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: At the moment I'm not getting outside as much as I should, I do enjoy gaming but it's hard to find time. I've been working 14 hour days all week! My boyfriend tries to tell me to switch off but it's hard when I know there's all this work waiting to be done.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You could try setting aside an evening or two a week for time with your BF. Just walk out of the office. Try to set some boundaries.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That might seem dangerous and risky, but sometimes it's important to set boundaries.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: If you don't do that, then the managers can just keep taking advantage of you and your work ethic.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yeah, he says the same kind of thing, that I need to be firmer and just leave when I'm due to. I guess the only way for them to truely see is for the work to just not get done as there's no time!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: From what you're saying, it sounds like you think you have no power. Is that true? Are you really powerless in this situation? Do not underestimate your power over your life.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I guess I do feel powerless, I feel like they never really listen to what I'm saying, they just act as if they are but then ignore me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like the managers are training you to be resigned to your fate. If they listen to you, it encourages you to complain. If they ignore you, you go away and leave them alone. However, if you leave work early (after 9 hours, say), then they might notice you. Are you willing to take a risk?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Maybe if I start acting more confidently they will start to listen.I feel like something needs to happen so maybe it's time to take a risk.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That's the spirit! Taking control of your own schedule is one display of confidence.
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I was in the store and there were two other women. They were whispering to each other and looking at me. I could hear a couple words and they were making fun of my hair and the way I dress. People just don't accept me. It's hard to feel so different.

dialog.text: Hello! How are you doing today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Is there anything you'd like to talk to me about?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Hello. I'm ok. How are you?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I am fine .. I am here to listen to your problems.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you. I am having problems with people making fun of my appearance. Why are people so mean?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I do not know - there are a lot of nasty people out there. Have you tried confronting people who are bullying you and asking them why?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Well, with covid, it's even harder to go talk to people. So, I don't think that's a good idea. I don't have a lot of money, so I can't buy fancy clothes. I don't think I can fix it.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You do not have to buy fancy clothes for the sake of other people! Maybe you could get some counselling to work on your self esteem though?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I see a counselor regularly. The sessions are virtual. I do wish there were some ways to figure out how to make the clothes I have look better or match better, be more organized with my wardrobe. I have a lot of problems with too many clothes that don't look good on me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Have you tried shopping in second hand stores? You can often get some nice stuff there for cheap.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: But really I think that the problem is your self esteem, not what you are wearing.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes! I love second hand stores! So I should not care so much what they say about me?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Right! To be honest I suspect that it's far more their problem than it is yours.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I agree. Those women were not even in shape. They had makeup, hair done, etc., but they were not nice women. Maybe they are just taking their problems and insecurities out on me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes I think that they were. I have had issues like this myself in the past and I know how much it hurts and how hard it is to overcome it.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes. It does hurt. I want to get better at picking clothes that make me happy. A lot of my clothes are baggy. Maybe I could learn to sew and alter them.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I went through a phase of wearing only baggy clothes because I thought i was overweight. Looking back I was not but I thought I was.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Anyway I hope I have been able to make you feel a little better! All the best for the future.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have had that same exact problem! When I wear clothes that fit nicely, I do get complements. I think I will go through my wardrobe and find the best clothes I have and wear those.Yes. It has been nice to talk to someone who has been through some of the same things.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That sounds like a great suggestion - good luck with it :)
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you. I hope you have a nice evening too!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: :) Can you press quit first? I am not able to :(
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Ok. lol. Thanks! Bye!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: bye!
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I recently found out that my best friend has lied to me about her whole life, and when I invited to my home she finally told me the truth after staying for a month ad we were fighting for the entire month she stayed.

dialog.text: Hello, how are you doing today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm sad and angry because I no longer talk to my best friend
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Do you know what might have happened to cause your and your best friend to not talk anymore?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Well she was staying at my house for a month and we were constantly fighting so she just stopped talking to me
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That sounds really stressful and I can see how troubling that is for you.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes it is and then she began avoiding me while we were in the same house, so we started arguing again and I found out she's been lying to me since I've known her and I'm very upset.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That's definitely very upsetting. I know how it feels to have that sense of betrayal from a friend I was close to for many years. However, I was able to discuss the issue I had with my parents and other friends. Do you have anyone else close to you that you can talk to?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I don't think so, my parents think I was too harsh by deciding to end the friendship, it as if my own family doesn't understand.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That can definitely add to frustration. What about your other friends? Do you have anyone who either shares the same opinion as you or does not know your friend that you can talk to?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: My other friend believed that it wasn't too harsh to end the friendship as they know I value honesty but it makes me feel angry that I was being used for so long and constantly lied to.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You have every right to be angry, but the most important thing you can do is find a good support system with your other friend. It will take some time to heal, but I'll tell you a paraphrased version of one of my favorite quotes: "Resentment is like swallowing poison and expecting the other person to die." It's important to find support in your other friends and heal properly.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I really love that quote, it's absolutely true; I think I will talk to my friend about the situation some more so I can fully get over it.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, I also realized that I wasn't angry with my friend but rather myself
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Can you elaborate more? Earlier you said you and your friend were arguing while she was living in your house, then she stopped talking to you. Why might you be angry with yourself?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Because I basically allowed her to use me for seven years and kept lying to me or gave her space because I thought I was being a good friend.I feel like I was stupid to do that and soft
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: If I may, I would argue that your actions don't make you soft and they certainly don't make you stupid. They are certainly not any reason to be angry with yourself. If I may bring up another cliché: "Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me." I would say you're in the "fool me once" stage and it is your friend's actions that have brought you pain. I think you're unlikely to trust her again.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Also, hindsight is 20/20. What you might see now in ways that your friend might have used you are things that you might not have seen then. We want to think the best of our friends until they prove us wrong. I think you were being the best friend you could be.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you very much, I'll continue to talk about the issue with my other friend, I really appreciate your wisdom.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Of course. I think you'll be alright and remember the healing process can take a long time after betrayal. Remember to be kind to yourself and keep that support system of your other friend by you.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No thank you, enjoy the rest of your day
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You too!
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I have a friend who is struggling with alcoholism. They try to quit and then  end up going back.

dialog.text: Good afternoon, what can I help you with today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have a friend who is an alcoholic and just can't seem to quit drinking.They quit for a couple of weeks but always seem to go back.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm sorry to hear that, that is a rough situation to be dealing with.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: What's very important for you to know is that you cannot control another person's actions.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: It is. I care for them a great deal and do not like to see them this way.I just do not know how to help them anymore.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It's difficult for those close to an alcoholic to watch them destroy themselves.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I will tell you that you can only take care of yourself. And you can only be honest with them about how their actions affect you.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: He is a wonderful person when he isn't drinking, but is argumentative when they drinkI do, we have talked over and over about how this affects both of us. And he cares when he is sober, but it doesn't seem to be enough to keep him from going back.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You may need to take some time away from the friendship then. To show him you are serious that you can't tolerate the behavior any longer.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I get that, but I am the person closest to him and he needs my support
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That's understandable. But if you continue trying the same solution over and over again, but are getting the same result...
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: true, but I do not think that not being here would help. it would only hurt him
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: In that case, you should be sure to shore up your defenses and be prepared, because it will be hard. You are a good friend, but don't lose yourself to save him.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Consulting some literature for friends and family of alcoholics may be useful as well, Al-Anon or something like that.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is a good idea. I do worry that he would be upset if I shared this with others he might knowHe is a really sweet person and worth the effort to help.he had a lot to give.has
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You should be able to find online Al-Anon groups, too.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm sure he does. Don't forget that you do as well.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I had not thought of that. I thought you had to go to the meetings and that would be hard for me to do.I will definitely look into that! I appreciate the suggestion!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It looks like they do offer online chats: http://al-anon.org/al-anon-meetings
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: And thank you for saying that I have things to give, I forget about myself in this sometimesThank you so much for that information. I had no idea!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: So much like this chat here, you wouldn't even have to give your real name, nothing identifying, just support for you. Supporting an alcohol is exhausting, and you will need resources.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: And a place to vent.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is sooo true! Sometimes I just cry because I do not know what to do anymore.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Try not to demonize your own frustrations, be easy on yourself when it comes to feeling upset with the situation, and continue trying to let him know that he hurts you when he behaves like that.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Having a person to let me know I am not alone and give some support would be very helpful!That is great advice! I am going to look into that.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Absolutely :-) I hope that it helps. You sound like a very kind-hearted person, and I understand that your situation is complex.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Just remember that you are as deserving of relief as he is. They always tell you on an airplane to put on your oxygen mask first, then others in your group.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: And thank you for reminding me that I matter too! It helps very much! I can't thank you enough!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm happy to hear that, I wish you luck and take care of yourself.
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I have gained about 30 pounds in the last twoyears. I am very unhappy with how I look and I actively avoid food and wait until I am about to pass out to eat. Yesterday, the first time I ate was at 7pm.

dialog.text: Hello, Good day to you
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Hi
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Is there something you wish to discuss today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, I am experiencing a lot of depression lately due to my weight and my boyfriend
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: If i am to understand you are having troubles with your weight and this is effecting your relationship ?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I to have experienced troubles with my weight, if can be a very troubling issue to deal with.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: thank you for udnerstanding
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Could I ask if you are currently participating in any activities or diets to manage your weight ?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am dieting but I mainly just avoid food and eat once a day. I am on depression medication which also reduces my appetite and I drink a lot of coffee to help surpress my appetite.I usually only eat dinner and a small snack
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Research has shown that if you eat at regular meal times the body can regulate your weight better. The trick is to consume less than you use in a day. To manage this its better to eat your recommended daily amount then exercise so you are using up excess energy
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I know but I am just so unmotivated. Sometimes I wish I could lose all the weight and then start the good habits to maintain
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes it is a difficult challenge.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Have you looked in to local support groups which can help you with motivation?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Not really - I do follow a lot of vegan and health groups on RedditI do eat about 1200 calories a day which I know is the bare miniumum but I have noticed a difference. I just need to start exercising more.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Thats good, I would suggest that you either join a local group or sign up to a online one. Maybe try one that includes meal plans for the week, support chat group that can motivate you.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes that seems like a good idea thank you
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Exercise is key to weight loss, maybe go for walks with your boyfriend. this will also give you time with him.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is actually a very good idea - we have a puppy and he is struggling with weight gain tooI definitely feel that we should start doing that
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: depending on the dog breed then puppy will need upto multiple walks a day. So its a great time to start walking then you can move up to a run
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That;s true she is a pug but she loves to run - I do miss running I used to run fairly frequentlyI am just struggling since I have broke metatarsals on both feet in a year - it's been a hard recovery
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I feel we have come up with some good ideas to work on over the next coming weeks. Is there thing else you would like to discuss ?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No I think that is good. I feel like I have come to a good realization. I know my ways are unhealthy thank you very much
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: SOrry to hear that. Have you received the proper medical care for your injuries ?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes I didI couldn't walk for 3 month total and then had to wear a boot for another 6 months
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Great, i wish you a good afternoon and hope the best for you with all your ambitions
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: thank you!!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Good bye
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: Covid 19 stress with the added stress of the holduas

dialog.text: hello?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: hello, how can I help you?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm seeking some support. Specifically looking for advice concerning my depression
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: How long have you known you have depression?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I've struggled with depression my entire life. It's been especially difficult this year
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Because of Covid? So you know at least the cause of your depression?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, because of Covid. I have two small children both born with genetic disorders. If they catch it they could die. They're both now displaying signs of anxiety and that's worsening my depression because there is very little I can do about it.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That must have been tough for you. I know Covid is scary, however, I think you're a very careful parent so as long as you keep the routine safe, you can at least not worry too much about it
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm doing my best, as is my husband, but with the holdays here we're struggling to explain our decision not to visit family because we want the children to be safe. Our family is a combination of Covid Hoaxers and antimaskers sadly.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Now is not the time to please your family or anyone else. You did the right and responsible thing for refusing to visit them.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: May I ask how old your children are?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you for agreeing with me. They are nine and four.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: they might have been scared because of external forces, as in they might see you being stressed out. I think it's good to talk to them about the seriousness of Covid, but also explain them it's not unpreventable. By discussing, you can reassure yourself too
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Maybe. I'll have to give them a few days as my mother is very self centered and we just got into it last night, but I might give that a try
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I think you can also cut down on watching news, when it first began, I followed the news closely, however, I realized I felt depressed hearing new number everyday so I only update myself once a week now and I feel bette
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That's good to hear, maybe I should do that.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Having a family meeting with your husband and children as much as possible to share your feelings might also help quite a bit
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm not so sure. My husband's anxiety is worse than mine and I carry the mental load for the entire family. He's usually happier staying in the dark, otherwise it's too difficult to lift him up when he's depressed if I'm also depressed.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Then do as you think is best for your husband. I'd say focus the work on yourself first, you need to feel good in other to take care of your family
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is true. Thank you for the advice
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: you're welcome, I hope you feel a bit better
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: My friend has started to get into political conversations on Facebook and I think he is embarrassing himself. He's spouting all these talking points without ever showing any interest in them before!

dialog.text: Hello! How are you doing today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm good thanks but pretty frustrated too be honest. It's my friend who has taken to being a pain on Facebook
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm sorry to hear you are frustrated! I'm gonna do my best to understand and talk through your issue. :) Your friend is being a pain on face book in what way?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: He's all of a sudden got an opinion on everything and tries to pull me into arguments with other friends.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like he didn't use to blast his opinion in the past or include you in arguments, is that true?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is true yes. It's like the world has to listen to his opinion and only his matters and he won't listen to reason. It's very frustrating and it makes me not want to talk to him. My eyes literally roll when I see a post from him.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Oh I see! I get where you are coming from. I have a few friends that no matter how long you discuss, they won't let the conversation end unless "they are right." It seems like your friend doesn't like it when he is wrong?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Absolutely and I'm not sure how to broach this with him. I actually feel like it is damaging his reputation. Other friends of ours feel the same way. Not sure what to do?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Gotcha so not only are you frustrated with what he is doing, but you are also worried about his reputation! First of all, can I ask if he is just your friend online or if you hangout with him in person too?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That's correct. He is actually a close friend and I wonder what has changed recently to make him like this. I've known him for over 20 years.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Okay I see. From personal experience, the best way to confront someone who likes to do most of their confrontations online, is in person. Since he is so used to almost "hiding" behind a screen, his feelings will be more vulnerable and real if you discuss your concerns in person.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Actually I've never thought of it like that. Perhaps a couple of us can have a conversation with him in person. Honestly some off his views are disgusting. I think this needs to stop.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: A suggestion I would make would be to hangout with him in person, and bring up the issues that you and your friends have been seeing. But it's important to not make him feel overwhelmed. Almost like he is being "ganged up on."
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes that's good advice, I think we need to be tactful and raise it in the right way. Have you ever experienced something like this with a friend yourself?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I can tell that you care about this person as a friend, but you are worried that the way he thinks and talks may ruin that in a way. Make sure to let him know these concerns! It will show him that you guys truly are doing it out of love.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: And yes I have actually had a very similar experience! Let me explain
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Ok sure please do
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: One of my best friend's and roommate, had a very hard time separating friendship and roommate issues. It caused a lot of issues in the relationships with our friends. She had a tendency to discuss issues over text and didn't like doing it in person. But we realized, the problem with that is that you can't tell the emotion behind messages on a screen. But once we talked in person, our issues were solved because we could hear the intended emotions behind what we were saying
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yeah that's useful. I think you are right in that the ambiguity of social interaction online makes him more inclined to say extreme thinks, perhaps to get a reaction. The more I think about it, perhaps this could be an indication that there is something he is dealing with and may be lashing out.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes exactly. It sounds like he might have other reasonings behind his actions. And you guys talking to him as friends in person, would show him that you care and that he is in a safe environment. He doesn't need to be so extreme
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yeah I think that's definitely the way forward. Listen this has really helped so thanks for the suggestions and sharing your own experiences.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes of course! I wish you the best in overcoming this hard time with your friend. I believe that you guys will be able to talk through it since it's a newer issue. :)
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I hope so too. Nice to talk to you and thanks again.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Of course! Have a good rest of your day
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thanks
dialog.speaker: seeker

situation: I do gig work and haven't had much employment since the pandemic started. Loss of money has me down.

dialog.text: Hello.
dialog.speaker: seeker

situation: I came off of my anti depressants and regret the decision.

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I have had trouble sleeping in the past and sometimes I still do, usually if it is when I'm nervous about the future.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: The number one way I have had to help my depression is to pray and read scripture. I don't know if you are a Christian, but that has helped me a lot. The second way is to have a good friend who will listen, not someone who will TELL me what to do or judge me, but someone who can empathize with me. A good listener is worth her weight in gold.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I've learned that mines not really an emotional thing. I feel like my sleeping issue causes my depression. Because no matter what- i always feel exhausted. Nothing has helped it besides medication. It just sucks always feeling fatigued and energyless. I actually did take up religion here this year to help with the coping that comes with this. It was very helpful for a while there
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: If I didn't get good rest, then I would definitely feel tired the next day and over time, it would wear me out. I believe medication will help with the symptoms, but it is important to get the root of the problem, why exactly you find it difficult to sleep.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Sometimes I take a benydryl because they always make me sleepy, but I usually know why I need to relax, I'm nervous about the next day. So I have found it important to know WHY I don't rest well, if that makes sense to you.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I plan on seeing a sleep doctor soon! Sometimes I lose sight of fixing the issue and need to be reminded. And yes!! I was treating my sleeping with Benadryl as well but it wasn't healthy to keep doing that.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm also thinking there are a few practical ways you can help yourself sleep. I was advised to get soft sheets, make my sleeping area more restful, make sure the time before bed is relaxing and calming.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I also was helped a lot by a Christian Preacher, he's long dead, but he has audio on youtube -- Frank Hammond, Pigs in the Parlor. It's a 5 part series I found helpful, you might want to jot that down. And I do encourage you to find a counselor, once you rule out the physical (doctor) then you can look at emotional, mental and/or spiritual. I think most of everything is spiritual and emotional to some degree, and our body just responds to that.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I always lose sight of how to make things better. It really helps to talk sometimes so someone can help me put things into perspective. I'll look into Frank Hammond! I am actually religious and would love to look into that.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I will definitely pray for you tonight because I know losing sleep is hard to deal with. We only have a few minutes here, but I'm pretty old and I have found this to be true so many times. Get a good support system of good friends. Having people who "get" you is SO vital to our lives. situation: I have been self-isolating since March which has made my chronic depression worse than ever. I live alone and have not touched another human being in all that time.

dialog.text: Things have much worse the last couple weeks
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It seems like things have not be great for you over the past couple of weeks. Why do you feel they have been worse?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I had been seeing a therapist online and two weeks ago he was really mean, but said he thought it was a good session and we were making a breakthrough. Then when I signed on last week I signed in to request entrance into the meeting and after a few moments was told it was denied. Nothing like feeling the person who is paid to help you refusing to talk to you
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That seems like a frustrating experience. What were your expectations of the session you were supposed to have? Did you feel like what you learned in your previous session would have helped you with dealing with what you typically work on in your mental health sessions ?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I feel like he didn't help at all. Up to that point we mostly just talked about politics or whatever. I'm a charity patient, he get's paid through the organization, but because of my financial difficulties, I'm not paying. I think he saw that as a shortcoming on my part.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I think that is definitely one way to look at it. But another way to look at your situation is you figured out a therapist who isn't worth seeing. That brings you one step closer to finding one who does actually help you. All you need to do now, is do some research and find someone who has your best interest in mind. Believe me, there are great therapists and terrible therapists. You just need to find one of the good ones now.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm not sure I can find another who I don't have to pay. My insurance has a $20 copay and if I had to pay that I wouldn't be able to buy groceries. This came through my religious organization and he was the only one available in my area. I guess I just have to find another way to cope
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: If you have financial issues and you need the help from a therapist you deserve the treatment. One thing you can do is apply for Medicaid and EBT. The state you live in will give you money to pay for groceries and to get help from a therapist for free if you don't have a high enough income. It may be worth looking into because all you really need to do is fill out some forms and likely you will be approved. When I was younger and struggling, this had happened to me and I received both of these benefits and it totally turned my life around. I think it can do the same for you as well.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm on Medicare and supplemental insurance. I didn't know you can, possibly, see one for free. I'll look into that. That is helpful.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Sure thing. What are some of the coping strategies you've been practicing with your prior therapist?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I asked him to help me with some but all he would say is that I should stop vaping (I switched from smoking some years ago). I told him it feels like I'm walking a tightrope and he's suggesting I get rid of the safety net without giving me something else, some other way to cope. He said that's not what a therapist is supposed to do and that my resistance shows I don't really want to change.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I can see how that comment he made would be frustrating. If you feel like vaping, you should continue to do; however, what happens if say you go somewhere and find yourself in a stressful position? What would be strategy you could use in order to recenter yourself? Strategies are important as they balance us when we experience stressors that through us off. Have you ever thought about meditation?

dialog.text: I asked him about meditation and if he could recommend something. He wouldn't. I have only been able to do it successfully once, at the meditation gardens when I visited my son in San Diego some years back. Since I can't always get to that kind of natural setting, I was hoping he could give me some resources. Do you know of any place I can find some?

dialog.text: Oh yes. Me personally, I like to scour youtube and find an environment with a sound I enjoy such as the beach. When I listen to that sound, I try to put myself by closing my eyes while sitting on the floor and breathing deeply for some time. It may be worth a try for you. I hope it helps you. Good luck!

dialog.text: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a breakI have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: HOw man classes do you have?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: many *
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have 6 classes

dialog.text: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! Maybe that might spark something in her to come up with her way of learning since traditional methods aren't working.

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yep! That's how I feel. What should I do to get back in good graces with them?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I do know people who have gone through the exact same thing in the past. When another animal attacks one of your fur-babies, it's absolutely terrible. However, the fact that this woman was given the option to either get rid of her dog or move tells me that you are 100% correct in the way that you handled this situation. It's unfortunate for the woman, yes, but she should have had more control over her dog. It's bad enough when one animal is attacked, but when it's more than one, that's when you really know that it's a problem. Again, legally, she had to make a choice, and that's because she failed to properly secure her dog. I really don't feel as though you did anything wrong.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: If I were you, I would ask to speak with the neighbors who have an issue with you face-to-face. I know it may be difficult, but I think that would be the best way to go about it. Are you on good terms with the other person whose dog was attacked?

I think everyone feels sorry for her.

dialog.text: That probably has a lot to do with it. I would feel sorry for her too, as it is very sad in general. However, it doesn't excuse the fact that her animal attacked two other dogs.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I've talked to the neighbors face-to-face and they just think that I overreacted. The woman started getting her dog and private training and so they feel that she was trying. My point was that my dog weighs 15 pounds and her dog weighs 45 pounds and, if it happens again, I may not have a dog anymore. I don't want to wait until a dog is killed or badly injured. I told them exactly what you just said, but they are being mean!I guess I could try talking to them again. Maybe they've cooled off some.

dialog.text: That is absolutely terrible. In that case, I would just tell them that you refuse to allow another dog to possible injure or kill your own dog, so you did what was necessary to protect your fur-baby. Had you not done anything, this could have happened again, and the outcome may have been much worse. At that point, if they still don't respond kindly, I'd tell them that you still feel as though you did what needed to be done, that you understand why they are upset, but that you will always do whatever it takes to protect your dog. Hopefully, they will stop being mean. Even if they just stop talking to you completely, it's better than them harassing you or something along those lines. If they do start escalating their nasty behavior, I'd let the manager of your complex know that you're being mistreated. I always try to keep things calm and quiet, but I refuse to be taken advantage of or treated poorly.

dialog.text: Personally, as I stated previously, I wholeheartedly believe that you did the right thing. If they're unable to see that, I'd try to just avoid contact with them unless it's necessary. I know it stinks and I'd be sad too, but unfortunately, some people just don't know how to let things go and seem to find joy in making other people upset. situation: My son is a recovering meth addict and has relapsed again. After two weeks of using he admitted himself back into rehab as he as done many times in the past without a lot of success. I am afraid it will be the same this time, that he will get out of rehab and then start using again.

dialog.text: HI, how are you today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am not doing well. I am very worried about my son's chances of recovery after so many relapses and frustrated because I know there is really nothing I can do to change things for him.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You must be very frustrated from feeling unable to do something.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am. He is a different person when he's not on drugs but when he is using he can get really mean and he scares me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I remember when my mother was having end of life mental declining issues. I understand feeling as if the person is changing and having unusual moods and mood swings.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Do you have anyone you can talk to?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I try not to think about the situation, because I don't see him since he lives in another state. But I can't get everything out of my mind. And yes I have my husband to talk to, that helps some. It's when I'm trying to sleep or when my husband isn't home that's the worst for me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You are feeling the way anybody in your situation would fee like. It must be helpful to have a husband who listens and can be supportive when he is there.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Have you always had sleep issues?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: It does help but he's as frustrated and upset as I am. I can't sleep at night for dwelling on everything and I don't know how to stop the thoughts about all the terrible things that could happen.When I'm upset about something I cannot sleep but if I'm in a good state of mind I sleep well.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Being upset can make someones mind race and make it really difficult to rest or get any sleep at all.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Have you ever gone through anything like this before?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes I've been dealing with my son's addiction and recovery and relapses for the last three years.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I can relate to being close to someone who is addicted. It can feel very sad and lonely at times. I would want to change the person in my life but just has to learn to let go instead. It is a process that takes years to learn.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am realizing that more every day. If it wasn't my son and just a good friend I would probably end the relationship but a mother can't do that to her own children, you know what I mean?And you are so right. I can't change or control him, I can only change and control myself and my responses to him. That is so difficult to do.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes, I understand how it can feel like our children are always our babies and we want to fix everything for them. Sometimes it feels like we can change them or re raise them if we just do more for them.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Have you had the chance to speak to a close friend or pastor about this situation?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Not really. Most of my friends haven't dealt with that so they don't really understand what I am going through, or even what my son is going through. But you're right, I have to learn to let go and let him fix his own problems with no intereference from me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You are very self aware and have good insight. I notice that you are very in touch with your feelings. You can use writing as a way to release emotions and express yourself, as you are now.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you, I will try that. Like a journal maybe?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes, I can recommend a journal on Amazon that I also use. Thank you for sharing with me today.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Please reach back out anytime.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you so much! I appreciate what you do!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Thank you!
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: Loneliness. Just tired of being alone and feeling isolated. This is the time of year when family gatherings happen, but I live alone.

dialog.text: Do you live alone? Do you mean meeting new people or getting together with people you already know? I am naturally an introvert, so it honestly didnt bother me the first month or so... but I'm so over it now. I wish I had taken advantage of freedoms we had before all of this.

dialog.text: I think it will pass eventually, but who knows when. It feels like every where you look things are falling apart sometimes. What kind of place do you live in?

dialog.text: Some people are on lockdowns, I'm nervous about our income in the next few months with the talk of more stay at home orders. I know it feels like itll be like this forever but I really dont believe it will. It may get worse before it gets better but I think things will go back to normal eventually.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I think we are in a long period of recovery because the country has too many laws in different states that are causing demands on the health system.

dialog.text: I have traveled states recently and the difference is crazy! I went through Tennessee, missippi, and alabama and stopped a few times.. some places are just going on like normal, hardly any masks.. in arkansas you never see anyone indoors without one.

dialog.text: Too much politics behand the virus and helping the people.Florida is mandatory, but Georgia is lacks. Tennessee is mandatory but other states are not as caring.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I totally agree. And you never know what is true or not. Its stressful. I'm in georgia now and most people do not wear them unless asked. I've only been required to at dr appointment. Is it mandatory where you are now?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No except at WalMartGeorgia has a high virus rate, yet no mandatory masks.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: There are signs here but half the shoppers dont wear them. I think people here dont fear it as much as other places.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: There is no mandatory requirement for the mask, especially at the convenient stores.You walk in and the employees don't even wear them. The screens aren't going to stop the spread.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: So you travel because you want to? YES the gas station closest to me.... I have been in there every other day recently and never seen a person in a mask. The employees at the dollar general close to me dont wear them either. I dont think it will either honestly. Sometimes I feel guilty if I'm not wearing one. The uncertainty of everything gets to me.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I wear mine for my own protection. What about you?I have to travel to Virginia soon and I want to arrive cleanI am only traveling now because of issues otherwise I would be in FLoridaI miss the bneaches
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I wear mine to protect other people.... I do have health issues that could complicate things but I dont thing it will stop me from getting it.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I MISS THEM TOO. We were in PCB last summer and everyone was freaking about the water lol. we had no idea what was coming
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I understand for protecting others, but when the people around you ignore the virus and refuse a mask, they aren't concerned about you.What part of Florida. I was near Stuart and Jensen Beaches.Masks are mandatory otherwise no entry at the stores
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: well I hope you are able to connect with people soon.. I think these are cool.. Its nice to talk to new. Youre right generally people dont care for other people, but I'm not that way. Panama City Beach.

dialog.text: new people*
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I care about others, but what good is it if they ignore your health.Hey glad yo chat. Catch you later.

dialog.text: Hello
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Is it possible to reframe how you look at your clients' dire financial situations?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I could try. It mostly gets to me at the end of the day

dialog.text: Some people can't do what you do because they don't have the heart to give someone else bad news. The reality is though, someone needs to fill that role and you do help people
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I am feeling very depressed due to work load

dialog.text: Hello
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Hi, how are you doing?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am not doing well. I am feeling very depressed due to work load and current household situation
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about it?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, due to COVID life is messed up. Work load has increase and more responsibility of household.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: COVID has really changed a lot of stuff. I understand your frustration. Has your work increased because of COVID conditions. Meaning you have to take extra work, or doing tasks that you dislike to do?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: If you don't feel comfortable elaborating, we can always talk about how you feel and how you can maybe feel a bit better.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Due to the furlough Company has increased my my work load three times. I am not able to take rest. Getting depressed everday.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That sounds really bad. I once worked in a company that placed unnecessary pressure on me, with a low pay. I can relate to how you feel. Do you have to depend on this company for work?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Sometimes it's really not worth working somewhere if it's really affecting your mental health.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: They are paying me well but It is hard to take the load beside I have family and kids responsibility. I don't have time for them.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I understand. But I want you to think about this. Your mental health is more important right now because it is affecting you. And how you feel really affects those around you, especially the ones who love you. If you take some time to think about what is more important to you in life right now can help you make a decision.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Working so hard can be a barrier right now. But you may have a bright future plan ahead. If so, that is something you want to look forward to.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I know what you are doing is really helping your family. And I know they really appreciate it, even if they don't say it.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I can understand that. But my job is really important right now as my partner lost his in COVID. and he is not doing anything right now not even helping at home. It makes me more low and it is hard to take care of 3 younger kids who are staying at home full time.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Ok, I understand better now. Thank you for explaining. What you are telling should to be something you need to discuss with your partner. Do both of you communicate well with each other? Maybe he is not aware of your situation or how you feel.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Nowadays he is so frustrated doesn't like to talk even. Whenever I bring household responsibilities or kids topic, he gets frustrated.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Oh no. I can see from his part he feels upset and frustrated because he may feel useless at the moment. But that's not an excuse to neglect responsibilities. I know it sounds kind of frustrating to do that, but maybe this small step on your half could also help him.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Do you have any family member that are close to you? If your partner isn't helpful, maybe seeking help from family can reduce your housework load.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Nobody lives near by. Kids are to young to understand. I felt bit good after talking to you. Thanks

dialog.text: I'm sorry if this did not help the situation. But I'm always glad to listen if you want to talk more.

dialog.text: It's a really tough situation, but you're a really strong individual. You've made it this far : )

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: No problem. I really wish you the best and I hope everything works out!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Crossing my fingers COVID ends soon.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Hope so. Byee take care

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Getting over a breakup will take time? Have you ever heard of DABDA? Denial (I can't believe this happened!) Anger (we all know that) Bargaining (If only I had done that, or if only - trying to make it FEEL better by imagining other scenarios - doesn't really work) Depression - sadness, then Acceptance -- we go in and out of these emotions and sometimes it can make us feel crazy, but all of them are normal in varying degrees and we don't know when they will happen.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No, but those sound like the typical stages of grief. I guess I'm in anger. I have no interest in barbagining.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I would make a list of things you have always wanted to do and then just BRAINSTORM any idea, no idea is too out there -- learn to ice skate, learn to play the ukulele, sign up for dance lessons, join the gym, go to a singles group at church, visit the elderly, volunteer somewhere.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I think I need to focus on exercise. Just get my body and mind healthy and full of energy. What do you think?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I also find it helpful not only to limit how much I dwell on my pain, but make sure I reach out to help someone else. I will tell you, that is the secret to happiness. Maybe help a neighbor with groceries or hanging lights. Old people (me) love help, bake something or call your aunt or uncle.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: True, but it's hard not to dwell. It's not like I have a choice. It overcomes me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I agree, get healthy and try to help others. One thing about feelings is that if you change your mind, you can change your feelings, it might happen slowly, but if you put your mind off of it, it will help. dialog.text: Time heals all wounds for sure
dialog.speaker: seeker
