dialog.text: yes, covid has made things messy but you can always connect with someone online and chat about what you have read so far. I did same thing during the lockdown
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That's what I can do. Thanks! It might make me feel better. What else can I do to control my anxiety?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: always make sure you get enough rest and when ever you are getting the feeling next time, distract your self with something you love and then continue after a while
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you so much for all your suggestion. Hope it will help me
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: and make sure you eat well. and exercise to control your breathing
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Is there any specific exercise?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: you can do bit of yoga and meditating. You should be fine with that
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you so much. I am feeling motivated now . I will try to start it tomorrow onwards.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: good is there any other thing i can help you with?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I think that's enough to start with. Hope it will work out. Thanks for all your help. byee
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: you are very welcome and good luck with your studies
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I am nervous and anxious about my status with my friends. I am not sure what I mean to them and if I am easily replaceable.

dialog.text: HelloAre you able to see my situation I typed?Is there someone there?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Sorry I'm here, please tell me you problems
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Just having problems with some friends. I feel like I am being left out.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Why do you think that way?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: They leave me out of planned outings from time to time. They also do not seem to care if I come or go when I am invited
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Have you asked your friends regarding this?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have not
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Okay, maybe you should ask your friends, let them know how you feel and see what they say about it
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Okay, I may try that. What do you think I should do if they are negatively receptive of it?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Under any circumstances, make sure you know you are not at wrong here.I hope it will not be the case but your friends might try victim blaming
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: So keep your stance and keep asking for the answer
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yeah, I don't want it to come off as an attack on my end. Maybe I should wait, see if the issue occurs continuously, note that it has been observed on multiple occasions, and then stand my ground?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm pretty this has happened a few times already, hasn't it?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: so you have every right to be upset and confront them, you shouldn't feel like you're attacking. You are just asking for what you deserve
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, but I feel like I need proof, you know? Like how you previously said, to make sure I am not in the wrongThat's true!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: What you need to do is note down the occasions where they exclude you and ask exactly what happened then
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Okay makes senseThen, I can ask like, was there a reason why I was not invited on this instance? Did I do anything to offend, etc
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes, that's good, ask them if you did something that offended them and why they excluded you. If they deny, then you can tell them how you feel. If they care about your friendship they will do something to fix
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is good advice. What is your advice if I still come out of the situation negatively (e.g. the friends do not seem to care about the friendship?)
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: honestly, I think you also know that if you care about someone and they feel upset, you'll do everything you can to help the situation. Therefore, if your friends refuse to acknowledge your feelings, I don't think you should be friends either
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I have had six people die this month, and I have been quarantined for 5 weeks with COVID-19.

dialog.text: Hello
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Hi
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: How is everything
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Not the best. I have been quarantined for 5 weeks with COVID-19 (tested positive), so I am getting cabin fever.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Ready for the holidays
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: So you tested positive, must be hard
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am starting to get an aversion to holidays. When I was in college, my father was dying, and Thanksgiving was the last meal he ate at the family table... Christmas was the last time he ate solid food, and he died on the day after EpiphanySo I have come to associate Thanksgiving through January as a time of loss.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: The holidays can bring back memories, but you have other family around right
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: This month has driven it home more, because I have had six people die this month. It's starting to bring on flashbacks.No, my family all moved from the area. The nearest is now half a country away and hasn't spoken to me in over ten years.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: The virus is hard. along with the season
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: It's been... interesting.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You must have friends around, right. have you contacted any
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: How long ago did your dad pass away
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Ahhh... I hate to be that guy, but I really don't have that many friends. I have a couple people at my church who have checked in, but I wouldn't go so far as to call them friends (we don't hang out, I don't get invited over...)I was in college. He died slowly and painfully. It was really unpleasant.And he was a brilliant man. I could only wish to be half of what he was.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That can cause loneliness as well. What about seeing if your family will chat and let them know you ae ok
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I don't even have contact information for them anymore. The last known phone numbers have been disconnected and the last time I sent mail, it was returned for wrong address, no forwarding information known.I think they forgot about me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Comparing yourself to others can be a positive and give you reason to strive more
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: The only one I still have contact with is my mother.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Have you checked to see if she is ok
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I avoid comparing myself to others. I usually come out on the bad side of it.I talk to her regularly. She is okay, but I fear she is reaching the age where I know I won't have her much longer.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: But use your dad as inspiration
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm just thankful I have had her this longThat I do. While I will never have the skills my father had technically, I am thankful that I did get his ability to be analytical and his compassion for others.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: See that is a positive thing. You both need each other
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is great to hear. He is a role model for you
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Absolutely. I still remember him teaching me things that I use to this day. I still smile when I think of one time when he first became ill and couldn't get out of bed...there was a project he wanted to do and it bothered him that it had not gotten done. Well, I was able to do it, because he had taught me enough to know what to do.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That is a positive in itself. Keep his legacy going through you
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: The look of pride in his face was priceless.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: And you have that memory to live by
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: The one thing I carry on because of him is my love for my church. He was on the church vestry (governing board). I am on my church worship team.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: His smile is in your heart and you can still feel him
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I actually made church history, because I sing with the praise team (some churches call that a choir), but I sing many of the songs in American Sign Language.I am the first signing member of the church.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: See that there in itself is a reason to smile
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: 2021 will be the 50 year anniversary of our congregation.I joined just over ten years ago.My church is my anchor.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You are a positive for your church. Not many can sign language
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: My pastor is wonderful. He is like the little brother I didn't have but always wanted.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That is awesome. See you have a purpose
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I imagine he is missing his big sister
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: My favorite story about signing in the church is how it began... I had asked to do it and had been shot down cold six times. Well, I laugh now, but at the time I was angry.If you mean me, I'm male.But the last time I was told I could not sign for the church, I told the elder who said no that God was going to give him a sign.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: But your determination kept your dream alive.sorry big brother
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: You are a very determined person. Don't let the fire die inside your heart
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Well, God delivered on the promise quickly. That same who morning we had a family visit who were on a road trip. They just were passing through but wanted to go to church while travelling.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: The Lord is using you to each others/
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: They had a little girl about 6 or 7 years old who was Deaf. She saw me sitting in the back of the sanctuary signing the lyrics to the songs, and praying in Sign. Her face lit up and she started signing too.At the end of the service, she found me and gave me a big hug around my legs and then looked up and said "I always wanted to go to a church where someone knew MY language!"
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: God placed you there for that little girl
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: From that point on, there was no problem with me signing in church.I think He placed her there for me, also. It was a mutual deal.There is no one in my congregation at the moment who signs, but I keep hoping for the future.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You have a calling on your life. Don't let the dream die
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No. That mission has been placed on my heart.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: He will use you in mighty ways
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Well... I should be going, but thank you for taking the time to chat.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Ok. Hope I was of help
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am a Christian also
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: You definitely were. I am feeling better than I have in about a mo nth. I appreciate that.God put you here tonight for a reason
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: God loves you.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Of this I have no doubt.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Glad iI was here.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am actually in the process of studying catechism with my pastor, and plan to be re-confirmed.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Live the dream and seek Him always
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I was confirmed in a different denomination as a child, but I learned nothing. One day I realized that I have no knowledge of the faith, and that did not sit well with me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Be Blessed for He lives inside of you
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: So I am changing that and not just paying lip service to Jesus, but actively seeking Him.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Are you saved
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Absolutely.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Seek Him everyday
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: He is my 1st in the morning
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I was not always. I drifted a few years back. My church family gave me a gift and sent me to a religious retreat at a resort owned by my church denomination. It was there and in that moment that I came back to God.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: God has away to bring His sheep back. He knew you and did not give up on you
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I fell away for 15 years, but He opened my eyes.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I try to go each year, as it's an annual retreat. I missed this year because of COVID, but hoping for next year. I was going to take a friend from out of state. He couldn't attend due to the pandemic. But if all goes well, next year will be different.It was about 15 years for me, as well.I was never far away, just not close enough, if you know what I mean.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Your a gift from God to the world
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I left my childhood church because it turned into a false church, and it no longer teaches God's word.I still pray for them daily that they can realize what they are doing, repent and turn it around.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: We were always close but He knew the time to bring you home
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Even though we are locked down can you sign online for a church
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: It took years to find a church that God wanted me to be with, but I have found my church family, and I love them. I am closer to my church family than I am to blood relatives.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Does your church have online services
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Due to technical issues, I can't sign for my church, but I do have the pleasure of streaming the service each week, so I can still see my pastor, hear his message, and worship.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: So you are still plugged in the church
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Because of the way the feed is set up, I can not participate unless I am at the church building, and I need to wait until I am clear of the COVID infection first.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: My church is miles away but I still hear the message every Sunday
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I watch the service live each week. Actually, I have told the pastor I have gotten spoiled and like the online streaming because I can watch the service again, later.There are days when I am closed up in my room wanting to feel sorry for myself that I take great comfort in watching the service again.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Can you send messages so the church knows you r ok
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I do, and my pastor is wonderful about chatting with me on Facebook every day or so.Just a couple weeks ago, he brought me a giant care package full of food and snacks to help keep me going and relieve the boredom.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: can you sign language the service and send it back for the church to reach others
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No... I'm not fluent enough for that. I do the songs because I can research them and practice ahead.I can't interpret.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Do u have away to record the service and sign language. Sign language the songs
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am blessed to have friends who give me technical advice. I have a friend who is a certified interpreter who has sent me video showing me the correct way to sign certain songs.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: So you have a way to sign for others.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: At the moment, I have no way, but that's okay. Since there is no one in the congregation who signs at the moment, I am not needed in that role.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You are Just like that little girl
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have no doubt if there were someone depending on me to get the message across, God would have shown us a way to get me streamed in.I will be where He wants me to be and serve Him as he chooses to use me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Ask and you will receive
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: True
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You are very gifted.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I just received a message saying our time is running out. But thank you. It has been wonderful chatting with you. God has used you to lift me tonight and remind me what it important. Thank you for that blessing.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Ok Be blessed. Have a Merry Christmas
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: You too, thank you.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Awesome and Good night
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: Currently going through a divorce because wife is cheating.  We just got married earlier this year.  I'm hurt and broken that she just switched me off.

dialog.text: Hi there, how are you doing right now?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: HI! Not good. I'm sad right now. I'm mad and angry all together.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: So you are not having a good time at the moment? Can you tell me a little more about why?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No I'm not having a good time at all. I am so mad at my wife for cheating and not giving our marriage a second chance.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Your wife has been unfaithful to you? I can understand why you are so angry about that!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Have the two of you considered counselling or are things beyond redemption now?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes she has been unfaithful. I think this person she is with is living with her now or staying there (I'm back in my home state now)
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I am really sorry to hear that. I do know personally how betrayed you feel when you are cheated on. All I can say is, it does get better.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I would love to try counseling. She won't even talk to me. I came back home to stay with my family for a few weeks. She called and said it's all over. I found out she has someone elseI have been miserable.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like you have been treated very poorly, do you agree with that?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes I have and everyone says to move on. I just don't know how to let her go in my head and heart.If she called me today and said come back I probably would go. I know I'm weak. I just love her.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Are there potential financial issues or do you think she'd be prepared to reach an amicable settlement?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No we just got married earlier this year. We never even got around to putting our finances together. So I'm good there. Thank goodness
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: She does not seem to have stayed true to her marriage vows for very long!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No and it shocks me because she was so against not getting a divorce. We think (her bff and sister) that she may be using drugs.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Wow that is very difficult. There are support agencies out there that can help the friends and family of addicts, I believe. Would you consider them?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I would. She won't even talk to me though. When I try to call and talk to her this other woman (the lady she's cheating on me with) answers her phone and will not let me talk to her.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That sounds really very controlling. Do you think that maybe she is regretting her decision but does not know what to do about it?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: She could be (at least I hope she is) but if she is there's no sign of that. She has never said or showed it
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Sometimes, unfortunately, you do just have to walk away from a mess if there's nothing you can do about it
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I know. I'm struggling with letting go of her. It's like my brain is consumed with the thoughts. I want to let her go. I just love her so much. I would of never married her if I wasn't in it till the end.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I hear you on that. Unfortunately some people do not take commitment as seriously as others. I have been in that position and had my heart broken.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes I agree with that. How did you get over it?I feel like she just turned her feelings for me off. She blocked me on all social media and my number. Then again I'm sure the potential drugs could help with her turning her feelings off
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Oh, I tracked him down and smashed his head in with an axe. Okay no I didn't really. I just told myself that I was better off without him and it was his loss. I am not sure I totally believed myself though.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: (sorry I had a temporary internet connection problem there)
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I keep trying to tell myself that but I don't really believe it either.It's okI think it just takes time. I am talking to someone that understands and wants to pursue me. But I can't let the wife go in my heart/head
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I would advise not to rush into anything else too quickly.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: You need to give yourself time to grieve before you move on
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: This person is ready and this person knows all about how I feel about my wife. I'm not going to rush into it but it is nice having someone that wants to be with you.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I hope that I have been able to be of some comfort to you!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes it's nice having someone to chat with. Hope you have a nice evening.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: And you too! Goodbye :)
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I feel depressed. I hate the holidays. I don't want to pretend to be happy around my family for christmas.

dialog.text: Hi how are you?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: HelloI am depressed
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm sorry you are depressed. What's going on?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I hate the holidays because everybody has to pretend to be happy even if they aren't
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Sometimes it can help to just talk about things and get it off your chest.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yea, sometimes
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Why do you feel that way? Could it be the people your surrounded by making you feel that way?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I always felt depressed. It is just worst during the holidays because people expect you to be happy and if you aren't, then they blame you for ruining their holiday
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I think everyone's off this holiday season. It's not a normal christmas. You're not alone in feeling this way.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yea, I suppose it's better that everyone else feels a little more depressed with me, I guessAt least this holiday
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Has anyone specific made you feel this way? I would hope your family doesn't make you feel that your depression ruins Christmas that's horrible
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Well, they don't understand. No, it isn't anybody specific. But, yea, they tend to think I ruin half of everythingThe start of the new year is rough too, because you have to start all over again with breaking your goals for the next year, but we don't really need to go there
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I think you need to surround yourself with more understanding people.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I agreeIt's hard to find those people thoughHow often do you feel depressed
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It can be challenging but there are understanding people out there. You can't always pick your family. But if they truly make you feel that way you aren't obligated to be there. That's horrible.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yea, that's true. I thought about going camping somewhere and wait Christmas out in the woods, but I don't know if freezing my butt off would be better than being with them all
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I have struggled my whole life on and off. Learning triggers and ways to cope with them is very important. A positive mindset doesn't cute depression by any means, but it will help in accepting ways to cope
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Anyway, we've been talking for awhile. I Thank you for talking with me. You seem nice.That is true
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You're welcome:) I hope you have a wonderful Christmas and can surround yourself with positivity. Wish you all the best
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you. I hope you have a good day.Oh, brother. We have to for another minute to get the full reward
dialog.speaker: seeker

situation: My friend Rick is a jerk. He's got an awesome new Corvette that he brags about constantly knowing full well I ADORE Corvettes, want one badly, and can't afford one. We've been friends for a long time but he insists on rubbing this in my face every chance he gets! He thinks it's funny. I'm wondering if I should just not be friends with him anymore...

dialog.text: Hey.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Hello, what's on your mind today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Just wondering what I can do to deal with my cocky annoying friend Rick and his new car(as above)
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: How long have you been friends?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: 30+ years since high school
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: And he has always had cocky attitude? Have you ever told him that?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: He has, and yes I've told him, he just dismisses it, thinks it's funny that I get jealous
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I understand your frustration, it's upsetting when they dismiss what you say even though you have been friends for so long.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thanks.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: What I would recommend in this case is, spend more time with other friends who appreciate you. You also need to tell Rick your honest thought, don't beat around the bush but let him know you're serious
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That's good advice! Thanks. I wonder how I can get through to him to really let him know I'm serious. Ideas?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I have been in the same situation myself, what I usually do is sit down with them and start the conversation in a serious mood. Explain everything I need to say and tell them that I mean every word. If they don't seem to accept and change, I keep my distance from them
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Makes sense. Unfortunately we live on the same street so it's kind of hard not to run into each other. :/
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That's even easier to make it clear, if you run into him, just give him a polite greetings. The point is, make it clear you have had enough
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Right, so basically let him know if he continues to act like he does, we're done as friends, correct? Or should I not be that bold?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes. Be not too harsh at first. I would say to give him 1 more chance. If he still doesn't respect your words, it's the best for both to say it clearly.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Sounds good, I'm looking forward to getting this resolved. Now I just have to work on the wording (what I'll say) to come across as serious without being too harsh, I guess.Suggestions welcome! :)
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You have the right mindset! Practice before talking will help you deliver your thoughts better.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yeah I tend to get too emotional lol
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I would start with something along the line "Look, I know we have had this conversation many times. However, i feel as though you never take me seriously. I want to say this one last time...."
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That's perfect. Copying that down right now!Seriously!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Getting emotional is totally fine, that's why you need practice
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: True it's just we've been friends for so long it would suck if we weren't anymore.So I've got a plan and know what to do. You've been super helpful! Thanks!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I understand, it's difficult to come to this decision when you've been friends for so long. I hope he appreciates your friendship just as you do and tries his best.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: We will see!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You're very welcome. is there anything I can do for you?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No, I think that's it!Much appreciated!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I think you can end our session here. I'm glad I could help a bit
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I understand completely. Depression runs in my family and if it goes untreated, can scare anyone that is involved. You can try suggesting that he talks to a close friend, family member, or counselor to talk about how he is feeling and ways to cope with it. Sometimes medication could be a good way to fix the chemical imbalance that can cause depression.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I will try to help him, he just doesn't want to seem to talk to my anymore. Do you have any suggestions on how to approach it with him?

dialog.text: You could start a conversation by saying that you just want to check on him and see if he is okay and how he is doing. You don't want to start the conversation by immediately telling him to get help, as he might just get defensive.

Once he tells you how he is doing you could mention that even talking to someone about his thoughts and feelings could lift a weight off his shoulders. If he seems that he doesn't really know why he feels the way does, you could suggest that medically speaking, sometimes our brains don't produce the chemicals that we need them to and it could make us feel bad. dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Oh well I understand your concern then. As a son or daughter it is certainly reasonable to be concerned about your parents especially as they grow older. I have a similar situation with my own mother.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I just don't know what more to do.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Well first of all, you have to take care of yourself because if you don't you can't help them. So just take a moment to close your eyes and take some deep breaths and realize you stressing is probably going to make them stress.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is helpful information. What can I tell them?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Well if you can get some concrete info such as from the CDC and John Hopkins showing case counts in your area. Show them graphs so they can visually see the impact. Also if you can get a hold of their doctor yourself, see if you can convince them to give your parents a call, say to check on them and give them some advice.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That sounds like a good plan. Is there anything else I can do to decrease the anxiety for me?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Don't get absorbed in the numbers, it can drive you crazy. Also if you are using social media like twitter and getting inundated with info, remember a lot of it is fake. I would suggest limiting exposure for a little while just to get you fixed a little bit, if that makes sense.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Do you think there are some good social media sites that could help?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Not particularly social media because it open to everyone, just pick and choose where you choose to get info from. The CDC is a great resource as well as the John Hopkins site which has been tracking since the beginning. Everybody has a couple of news outlets they trust, use those.

dialog.text: How can I cope with limiting my visits with my parents because I am afraid to spread COVID?

dialog.text: First of all you are not alone. but don't let them see you anxious for sure. You can also show them if they can how to do video visits. You can do that all the time, even phone calls every day. It means a lot.

dialog.text: That makes sense. I appreciate the suggestions. How can I show them the kids care too?

dialog.text: Nothing will make grandparents smile more than seeing their grandkids on a video call. If you don't want to bring them when you physically visit have them record themselves on your phone as an example.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Maybe I can send them some pictures too. Nothing like a great big hug, but for now some video chats and pictures or recordings may help. I'm starting to feel a little more relief.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Of course. I don't know if they dressed up for Halloween, but see if they want to dress up and take some pictures for grandma. Pictures and voice and video are wonderful in these times.

dialog.text: I understand what you are going through. It is as if you are being pulled in two directions, but are not sure which is the best option at the given moment. I think it is great that you wanted to go back to school, but if your heart is not in it, then it may not be what you should continue pursuing.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I know I want this though. I enjoy what I do and what I would do for my career if I graduate. I mainly feel inadequate. I feel that I am not good enough. I am willing to do whatever it takes but fear that whatever my "best" is may not be good enough.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I can feel your worries when you speak about your anxiety, and I am hoping we can find a way to approach your feelings. Do you think there was a specific instance that is causing doubts within yourself or is it in your nature to self-doubt?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: It is in my nature to self doubt. Additionally, I have had a few bumps in the road during my program and struggle to pick myself up after those bumps. For example, I am on academic probation and have a certain expectation over the next few months that I have to hit to stay in the program due to struggles in previous classes. I am reaching the bar just fine, according to those that I work with, and often feel I am doing quite well but occasionally I start to panic and think that I am not doing as well as I think that I am and start to spiral
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: This has also been a past struggle of mine, and I think it partially stems from the bar we set so high for ourselves. We obviously cannot reach the top right away, but have to work our way up. Often times, when facing an obstacle, such as a bad grade, we might retreat further down the path due to fear that it will keep happening. I know that I personally had a tendency to think of my family and friends who I feel are dependent on me or comparing myself with others when the only person we should think of in these instances is ourself. When making progress, tiny steps upward matter more than you think. But when we take a step backward, we cannot fall back down to the starting point by letting our doubts pile upon one another.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is a really good point and helpful. Thank you!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Of course, I am happy to help! I have noticed that letting yourself celebrate a good grade can be really helpful to feel that you are enough and making good progress. But when things do go south, because life certainly happens, we must stay in the present and live life like we usually would, with a drive that we are going to push harder against whatever we have to face next.

dialog.text: What type of things are you worried about during the pandemic?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That I may not find a job soon which is making me depressed

dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I have a problem with my preteen son.  Perhaps we have been together at home quarantine for too long that he just rage today, saying that he has no life while i told him that he need to at least finish up a math worksheet assignment.  This is after he already had 3 hours free video game time.  He yelled, I screamed.

dialog.text: Hello! How are you feeling today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Started out ok but now I am so angry and depressed
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Can I ask why you feel angry and depressed?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Can I ask why you feel angry and depressed?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: As I explained, had a fight with my preteen son.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like you are frustrated. Do you mind sharing what the fight was about?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I told him to work on maths worksheet and he did but not very concentrated. I tried to help him and asked him to neatly write out the formula but then he just started raging and yelling at me.Then he said he has no life after he had played video games for like 3 hours.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I am sorry to hear that you two fought! What made you feel that he was not concentrating on his homework?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Does he often struggle with homework?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: he just didn't like doing things sometimesbut generally is fine.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like you feel he has a loss of motivation towards school work, is this correct?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: no, he just didn't want to be told what to do.very emotional these days for kids
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Alright, so you feel he has an issue with following instructions? Have you ever tried disciplinary action like taking away video games when he feels he does not want to listen to you?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes I did. But no point, he just upset on things like didn't get to be with his friends, or having no friends, no life etc.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Do you feel he could possibly be depressed?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I think soBut so am I .
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It must be even harder during times of the virus!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I am sorry to hear that, have you thought about seeing a counselor through the internet?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: yes may be i have to reach out for his school counselerthanks for listening .
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I think that is a very nice idea. I also might suggest finding activities that you both could enjoy and spend time together. Maybe finding a show you both could enjoy will open up room for a greater connection!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: It could also help both of you feeling lonely during these hard times!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thanks... I need to find some motivation to do so as well...
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Do you have any self-care activities that you enjoy doing? This could help feelings of depression. Even taking some time out of the week to do something you enjoy can help lift up one's mood.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I don't have much hobbies but I tried to stay active like going to swim, doing yoga, reading books. So I kept myself busy already but more for the sake of getting my mind of things, like people playing video games and watching tv.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Well I am glad to hear that you have some activities you enjoy! In relation to your son, how do you feel when he plays video games constantly?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: He usually is ok but now is holiday I let him play more but got even worst!As if playing games made him even more depressed
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Have you ever thought about using the video games as an incentive. For example, if he finishes his homework, he can play for two hours or something?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes he usually only play after he finished all his homework on school days.But now school is out I just let him play whenever.But it doesn't make him happier
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It is good to hear that the video games did not get in the way of him completing his work. Do you have any other ideas as to what hobbies makes him happy or interested?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I don't know whatelse he wanted to do. It is like he didn't really have a preference.Thanks for listening.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I think starting with the school counselor is a great idea, I feel she will have more of an idea of how your son functions in school and maybe give ideas to helping his mood.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, no problem! I hope you can find a solution to helping your son.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thanks!
dialog.speaker: seeker

situation: I am at my first semester in a doctoral program and have a lot to do at once and have been feeling very anxious in the past few weeks.

dialog.text: Hello
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Good afternoon! What can I help you with today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I've been feeling a lot of pressure and stress lately due to school
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Oof, yes, school can be a tough situation. Are you close to the end of the semester?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That can be both a relief and stressful, because a break is near, but all the exams and projects are due.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, I am a little more than halfway done with the semesterThe thing is that I am in a doctoral program, so even though the semester is close to the end, I always need to continue working
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Ahh, I see. That is a great deal of time and work. What are you studying?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: It is... I am in psychologyI have to work on my thesis on the side even with all of my classes and I have a hard time managing my time and keeping track
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Time management can be very difficult with a normal class load, that sounds exhausting.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: It is!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Do calendars help you at all? I am a super visual person, so calendars and planners are invaluable to me, as well as different colors of ink and labels so I can visually divide my attention
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Getting a million different colors of pens and highlighters changed my organization for the better.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I do keep a physical and electronic agenda, but I feel like even if I write down my tasks, I find a way to procrastinate which is what I am having trouble with
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Also, setting clear boundaries for your study/work and relax times may help. I like to set a timer for, say, 45 minutes, and work/write/read/study for that long, then, I get a 10 minute break. I'll go outside, refresh my coffee, grab a snack, dance to some music, stretch, then set another timer for 45 minutes, then another break for 10 minutes. That allows my brain to take a second and refresh from the work.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is actually very helpful, I'll take note of itI think it would help to fix break times so I can actually focus on working
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Or, like, today, I woke up and spent half an hour allowing myself to drink my coffee and scroll through Reddit. Then it was time to work on my group project for 45 minutes, then a break, then I worked again, took a break, went to a class, etc. Scheduling your breaks can be helpful too so your lizard brain doesn't freak out and go "WE ARE GOING TO BE WORKING FOREVERRRR"
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I agree!!! That really is helpful, thank you
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: which, for me at least, is where the fatigue sets in. You're very welcome! I hope I was helpful. You seem positive and willing to try new things, and I think you will be successful even if you are tired.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: The pandemic hasn't really helped eitherI'm always locked in my apartment and staying sitting down in front of my computer all day
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Definitely not. Everyone's Maslow hierarchy getting knocked out from under them is extremely disconcerting.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Hahaha, Maslow, i like it.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Like how is a person supposed to study, self-actualize, when we literally don't know what will happen next?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I agree! I've also been turning to drugs a lot lately due to the situation. Procrastinating makes me feel guilty, and I end my day too early to smoke and focus my mind on something other than studying....
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Are there aspects of your study that you dislike, or are you just ready to be done with school? Little of column A + column b?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Hm, I think it has less to do with liking or disliking, and more with starting a very hard and lengthy degree online without any social contact
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Ah, yes, that makes sense. And working from home is infamously hard, again, for lack of boundaries, so in addition to just not seeing people and getting the casual affirmation and confirmation messages on a daily basis of like "hey Jim you did a great job on that spreadsheet" or "Haha Jessica you're so funny", we also are writing papers in our pajamas and bedclothes, which makes it seem interminable.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Ugh exactly
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Listening to lectures while the doorbell is ringing and it's just so strange and we aren't set up to do it. That's why I'm a big fan of specific spaces in my house since March. I tried to sit in bed with my laptop and do things but 1. I'm old and it hurts my wrists and 2. my headspace is so completely different from being my computer chair and at my desk. I try to be really strict about where I do my work., maybe trying to structure that a bit could help you feel a little more in control of the work load and your day's schedule.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I agree, that makes a lot of sense! Thank youYou have been a big help today and I really feel listened and understood. I really appreciate it
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I am very glad to hear that! You sound motivated to succeed and I think that you deserve to take care of yourself and stay healthy to complete your studies. It will be hard but it will also be worth it, and you should be proud. Good luck with everything!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Wow, thank you!Have a great day
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Thank you! You too!
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I found out that my boss has not been paying me accurately.   I am so upset because I don't know what to do.  I feel like I should quit.

dialog.text: Hello, how are you doing today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Hi there. I am not doing very well today. I am really angry.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm sorry to hear that you are feeling angry today. Tell me more about that.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I recently discovered some discrepancies in my paycheck. I am not sure what to do to correct the situation. I am just so upset right now.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I can definitely understand why this could make someone upset. What are you considering doing about the situation?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I'm not sure. I thought about quitting but I have been working there for over 7 years. I haven't even told my boss yet.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That sounds really tough. Sometimes people who are in your situation find it comforting to talk to someone they are close with . What do you think about this?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I think that could be helpful. I might call my sister and ask her advice. It is probably not a good idea to quit my job.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like your sister might be able to help you figure out this situation. It can always be helpful to make a list of pros and cons about the situation. You originally said you were angry because of a discrepancy with your paycheck, but on the other hand it sounds like you are considering quitting your job altogether. What are your thoughts about this?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Wow that is a great idea. A list of pros and cons might help me decide if I should stay there. I think I will make one today. I also need to tell my boss. Maybe it was just a clerical error. I hope I'm not reading too much into it.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It always seems easy to read to much into things. Another suggestion is to think about how the clerical error happened. Was it because of your boss? Or perhaps just an accident?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is what I am unsure about. I think I have to tell my boss so they can look into this issue. I hope my sister is able to give me some good advice about what to say!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like you are wanting to tell your boss about this. How do you imagine you will go about telling your boss?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I think he will be apologetic. He has always treated me fairly. It is difficult for me to put my anger aside sometimes, which is why I have not said anything yet. I am afraid I will not remain calm and might say something mean to him. That would be terrible.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like you are nervous about saying something mean. What do you think would be helpful for you to do do in order to prepare? Some people in your situation might find it helpful to role-play with someone.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes! That is a wonderful suggestion! Maybe I can ask my sister to pretend to be my boss when I talk with her. I mOOPS! I mean to say I'm sure she would be happy to help.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That sounds like a great idea! Then when you actually talk with your boss, it will be easier since you already talked about it with your sister.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes you are right. I am so glad you suggested that! I think the pros and cons list will help me a lot also. I feel less angry now that I have a plan. :)
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like you have a great plan in place! I'm glad to hear you are feeling less angry now! :)
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I was so angry, I could not see the situation any differently. Thank you so much for helping me make a plan.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I can understand how you feel. Sometimes I let my anger get the best of me, but it is always important to remember to stay calm and think about your options and have a plan!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I hope things go well for you!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: And don't forget about asking for help! Sometimes that is the hardest part.Thanks! I hope so too!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Absolutely! Always asking for help when you need it is a great idea.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I know you will two will be able to work through this together

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: youre right

situation: I am extremely stressed with work and am very unhappy.

dialog.text: Hello
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Hi how are you?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Im not doing very well at all.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: What's going on?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am very stressed out with my work.I feel like I am being over worked but I also feel stuck at this job.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I know the feeling. what do you do for work?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am a lab assistant.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: how long have you been in your role? and do you have any coworkers that feel similar to you that you know about?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have been in this role for about a year. I am the only one at this level. I take care of a lot of the productivity and logistical work. Im just really stressed recently
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Somewhat similarly I'm in a supply chain role, for a year now, and the only one at my level too. I often feel like I'm alone in my job and that I manage my boss... It's pretty frustrating.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: is there anything that makes your job less stressful?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I think that being able to have a better work life balance would help but I have a hard time talking to my boss.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: do you think your boss would be receptive if you did talk to them? or would they dismiss your concerns?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am unsure. They are very much all about work. I am afraid they wont see my point and understand my want for a better work life balance.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: This has been a pretty hard year for everyone. however you ultimately gotta do whats best for you.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Have you considered searching for a new job?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have but it is hard to find a job at this time. I also really like what I do but wish I could have more balance. Do you have any advice for how to balance stress at work and your life outside of work?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm in the same boat. I would say, the things that work best for me, are to take breaks during my work day and go for walks or as soon as I'm done with work I force myself to go for a walk. I find moving helps me feel better. I also use that time to think about how I can look for a new job or rethink the things that are bothering me
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: maybe you can try something similar?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I think I could try that. I have a hard time detaching from work especially working from home. I feel like I never really 'leave' the office. I am always working even when I normally wouldnt be.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Change the scenery, it'll help! plus movement releases endorphins which make you feel better.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you! I will try that.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: no problem!
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: We were engaged, and now all of a sudden we are not.

dialog.text: Hello there, how are you today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Hello. Better than usual. What about you?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I am good thank you. Is there anything you want to talk to me about?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes. Recently, I broke up with my fiance. And no matter how much I tell myself that life continues, I still feel like there is a void inside of me ever since it happened.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: So your relationship ended and you feel that you are struggling to get over it, is that correct?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yes, that's exactly right.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I am very sorry. I have been through something like this myself in the past so I do understand.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: How long did it take you to get over it?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I think it was at least a year before I felt truly myself again and that I was able to enjoy life
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That gives me some perspective.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I can tell that it's all very raw to you at the moment. You really need to step away and give yourself some time to heal
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I am not sure if I can leave my obligations behind.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: What sort of obligations do you feel that you have? You need to be kind to yourself at the moment
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have a job, and my siblings are not doing too well, so I have to make sure their stuff is taken care of, or else my parents will end up babying them, and my parents are not in their peak health. This is not something I can afford to step away from.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It is good of you to be so caring and responsible towards your family. Do you think that perhaps you are taking too much on yourself though, especially at such a difficult time?

dialog.text: It might be so, but the sad truth is that when people don't fulfill their functions, someone else is going to have to do it for them. Maybe tho, I could fix my schedule to where it allows me to have firmer boundaries.

dialog.text: I think that that is an excellent idea and that you are being very mature about this.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Are you in contact with your ex at all?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: No, I made a commitment not to contact him.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That seems sensible. I had a problem with not contacting my ex when we split. I kept wanting to talk to him again even though I knew that I should not
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: What made you stop?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: A restraining order :D
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: This actually made me laugh :D Thank you for elevating my mood
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: In all seriousness though, with hindsight I realise that our separation was for the best. I think and hope that you will realise this in time too
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Thank you. Your analysis is extremely helpful.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You are most welcome. I really hope that things start to go well with you soon.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: My friend's husband is spreading false rumors about me because my daughter moved up in soccer and his didn't. He is saying I'm having an affair with the coach, who is married!  I am NOT and my daughter happens to be a much better soccer player.  I do like his wife but this is unforgiveable.

dialog.text: what should I do?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Can you tell me a little more about your situation so I can better understand?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: My friend's husband is spreading false rumors about me because my daughter moved up in soccer and theirs didn't. He's telling people it's because I'm having an affair with the coach - who is married! This is not true! My daughter is a better soccer player.what do you think I should do?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It sounds like your friend's husband might be jealous of your daughter, or embarrassed that his daughter did not get moved up also. Have you spoken to your friend about this?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I haven't yet. I was deciding whether or not to talk to him directly or just her or both at the same time. I am really upset and don't want to lose her. I know people get all crazy about their kids and sports. I agree that he's jealous but his daughter isn't really that good - didn't make the school team either. Should I talk to my friend alone first?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It depends on the depth of the relationship between the three of you. How long have you all been friends?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: About 6 years. Our daughters are also friends, too. I am single so I don't care about the husband but also don't want to come in between their marriage.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes, that is a difficult situation to know how to handle. It could be in your best interest to leave your friend out of it so she doesn't feel stuck in the middle or forced to take sides. However she could view the opposite as you going behind her back.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: yes that's true. I don't want to go behind her back but also don't want to get her involved. I could have the coach talk to the dad maybe?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Yes, coaches are a great resource for life's dilemmas. Perhaps another option would be to casually mention something to him in passing, like at one your daughters games as to avoid any big blowups or emotional exlosions.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Oh that's a good idea - in public and not making a big deal about it - and before she moves teams and rumors get worse.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That is exactly right. Each person handles and avoids conflict differently and you have the important roll as leader in all of this. There is a chance he is not aware of the strain this has put on you emotionally and he could respond well to not being called out by someone else. Does that make sense?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: it does - but doesn't seem that he cares about my strain on my life since he's the one spreading such lies about me. I just hate him!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I can understand how you would feel like he doesn't care about the strain it's placed. Can I ask, are your daughters aware or involved in these rumor's? This could make a difference in how you could respond.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I did tell her because I was so mad when another mom told me. She doesn't care. She still likes the friend but not the dad.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Sounds like your daughter has a good head on her shoulders. Maybe there's something to be learned from her reaction to all of this. I understand how hard this has been for you so perhaps simply ignoring the rumors will allow you to heal quicker, by simply being the bigger person. Because rumors are just rumors, after all. You and your daughter know the truth and that's all that matters.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: yes you're right. I will try to just ignore. And figure out what to do with my anger over all this? Maybe go for a run and also avoid him?
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: If he knows you know and you rise above with a smile on your face, that could show him that you are more mature than his childish games, and that you mean business. By taking ownership of your own feelings and emotions, you might find that will squash your need to let out any anger towards him.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: oh I like that and I am willing to try. I am tired of wasting my energy being so angry at this man who like you said is jealous which is HIS problem and shouldn't be might, right?!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Exactly. Let his problems remain his. You worry about you and your daughter and he can watch from a distance confused at his failed attempt to reflect his own dissatisfaction with life onto you didn't work. I think you will feel freed of any stress this has caused.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I really like that and I hope I'm able to do that!! Thank you!
dialog.speaker: seeker

situation: I am struggling with my law school exam prep. I'm not sure if I can make it through law school

situation: I just have no energy and feel helpless about current events.

dialog.text: How are you today?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Feeling down.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I'm sorry to hear that, what's got you down?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I live in a more rural area that has moved into our highest risk tier for Covid. They just seem to be making all the wrong choices amongst our local schools and other agencies.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I can relate to being in a rural area being hit right now. What are the wrong choices that they're making?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: The middle school is still in person 100% of the time. There have been >30 cases, most in the last 3 weeks, and they keep sending letters home stating that they don't believe the kids are getting sick in school. It's infuriating.So, I get mad, then I get anxious, then I get down...
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: It's such a hard time right now, knowing what is the right thing to do. Does your district offer any virtual options?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: They do. It's a pretty poor one though. I'm looking at charter options right now. They only offer ELA, Math, Science, and SS through the public virtual option.The kid I'm concerned about is taking math 3 grades ahead and high school spanish. I do not think their program is in her best interest, so I'm focusing on the charter option, but it takes time :(
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That's frustrating, obviously you want what's best for your kid and it's going to take time.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: It does. Like you said, crazy time for everyone.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I think the important thing to remember is that we're all going through similar things. Which probably increases our anxiety because we don't have any good way to express our frustrations since everyone else is in the same or worse position.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: True, true. It does help to focus on how you can help, especially if you find people in worse positions.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: While we're busy worrying about things like education and jobs, I like to look for the little messages of hope and empathy that we'[re seeing through all of this as well. It's a good teaching moment for our kids and showing how to collectively work to take care of one another.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I like that. I especially like the idea of involving the kids.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Just think of all of the ways our kids are learning to adapt to different life situations as well. That's worth just as much as their formal education. Your concerns are valid, and hopefully finding another safer school works out and this whole thing is over soon.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I have been trying to do projects at home I normally wouldn't to try to help everyone fill time. Things like creating websites, art projects, and such. Those skills will help tremendously.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That's a great idea, helping fill time with things to distract is a good way to relieve stress as well.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: So, I guess I'll just keep doing what I can and try to stay away from media and the state's tracking site. I had been doing this, but the announcement for the new tier came from the school!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: What region are you in? We're midwest and watching the news is not the best way to lighten the day.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Midwest. Not the worst place to be, although we supposedly hit some statistic that no other state has yet, so we may be heading that direction.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Well my suggestion is to turn off the news.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Consider it done, lol! I'm gonna log out now, but you did give me a couple points to consider that would be better than dwelling on the hopelessness.Stay safe where you are.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You too, thanks for chatting!
dialog.speaker: supporter

situation: I hate looking at myself in the mirror, every time I do I feel like the ugliest person in the whole world. I feel like nobody will ever love me.

dialog.text: I hate the way I look. Everytime I look in the mirror I cry

dialog.text: When I look in the mirror, I think Im the ugliest person in the world sometimes

dialog.text: How old are you if you don't mind my asking? This is a common thing among young people.

dialog.text: I am 32

dialog.text: Or have a new haircut or something :)

dialog.text: I like that idea too, I will give it a try

dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: That is kind of you to say, thank youYou have helped me quite a bit today, I appreciate it

dialog.text: So, what sort of clothes do you think you are going to buy? :)

dialog.text: I like doing my makeup and getting dressed up, even if I have nowhere to go

dialog.text: That is a good thing to do .. great for the self esteem. Maybe buy some new jewellery too?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I like the idea of pampering myself. That is something I don't do too oftenand I need to do it more. Perhaps I will feel better then
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You need to indulge yourself from time to time :) Get yourself a nice bottle of wine too. Though maybe not chocolate :D

dialog.text: Anyway I hope you are feeling a little better now ! Thank you for talking!

dialog.text: Thank you, you too!
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: (I can't press quit my end so you have to first :))

situation: overall daily stresses

dialog.text: Hello I am here to talk about my overall daily stresses
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Hi! Tell me what's going on.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: yeah I guess different factors, just self isolation for months due to the pandemic, and nearing the end of my studies and experiencing that final last-minute crunch with studying and assignments.I am more stressed and anxious than anything, and not really depression.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Understood. You have a lot on your plate, especially with the "new normal".
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: yes that's right. The plate issue is more to do with my studies now than the pandemic.Though the pandemic is adding to my anxiety and fear of the outside worldespecially when I have to go out everytime for errands and personal admin.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Are you doing online schooling? And yes, going anywhere can be a bit nerve-wracking
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: yes I am. I preferred the old-school way. I've completed university before and it's much better to do things in-person. My online studies have been in place even before the pandemic.Just finishing up with courses and catching up with last minute stuffI feel like so little time when in fact I had loads of time for the last few months.I just seem to think and do things slower and more distracted
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I understand; sometimes I have moments like that, too.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: like time is moving on so quickly and there's so little hours in the day but I feel that I don't do enough in a day with my school, kind of distracted or wasted time and then when I do something, I look at the time and am sometimes surprised at how much time had actually elapsed when it felt like I didn't do much.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: What kind of things are you doing for yourself? Do you have a place to or a thing to do to...decompress?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I think this has to do with the pandemic at the start of the year and that changed my momentum and rhythm in life and coupled with social isolation, which puts a damper on my studying mentality, I think.I spend tons of time at home nowadays. I try to surf the net and read up on stuff, and that takes a lot of my time, and kind of aimless, and what I would say is procrastination. I work out from time to time, but not as much as I used to before the pandemic.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Sure, it sometimes feels like time is different right now. Like your typical life patterns just did a complete circle.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I wanted to set aside hobbies and things to develop, like writing during the pandemic, and improve on that skill, but I never got to do that. And now so many months have gone by, and all that's on my mind and plate now are my studies, because it's like I do things slower and leave it till the last minute, even though I know I can pass, but just not as good a mark as I would have liked and not my usual work and study ethics from before.yeah not only a complete circle but to me, it's like an aimless road to nowhere, and it goes on and on and repeats day after daythat's how it felt for the last few monthsand everyday is the same and at home, and only two months ago I started working in a new part-time position and that got some normalcy back and less stress and alleviated unpredictability with the economy for me.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Understood! I'm not in the exact same situation, but I feel you. There's the thought there would be so much to do things and...there's not. And you feel stuck a bit.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: stuck for sure. It still amazes me that it's november and not march, because it still feels like that.and nowhere as festive, fun, and alive as last november. It's a huge change
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Definitely a massive change!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: it feels nothing special, and not normal, and not even like a real november, you know? It's like even if it's christmas, I wouldn't ackowledge it's christmas even though it is, because of the changes and we can't do the things w e used to do.hopefully, scientists can study all these phenomena and our physiological, social, and mental responses to the pandemic. There will be so much that can be learned from all this, I feel.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Of course. We can'r celebrate the way we used to, we might not be able to visit family. Oh yes, this is a learning opportunity about anxiety and isolation
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: And it's worse because I live by myself so don't have someone here. But I do talk on the phone with my friend daily about things and that does help a lot.yeah like for me, I am not able to fly back to visit my folks this year, and this is the first timeAnd I feel bad about it but nothing I can do
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That's good that you have people to reach out to.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: yeah anyways, thanks for listening and understanding. I appreciate your input very much.It does help for me to vent I guess and for someone to listenI am good to go nowthanks a lot for your help
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: You're welcome! Venting can be great! Take care of yourself and stay in touch with your friends
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: will do. And best of luck to you. Stay well and stay safe. Thanks again.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Thank you. Have a good day and take care.

situation: Just failed a huge test in my class and may not graduate this semester

dialog.text: Hello

dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Oh no! I can totally understand why you're stressing over that! Absolutely valid reason for anxiety.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: May I ask how much of the whole grade was the test's percentage?

dialog.text: Yeah it's really weighing down on me. It's the only thing I can think about. The test was worth 75%

dialog.text: What was you're score?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: I got a 62% on the test.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: That isn't TECHNICALLY a failed grade by the standards of most professors. Albeit a low grade, it's a D. Anything below 59% would qualify as failed.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Yeah, but taking into account my scores on homework, I don't think it's enought to pass the class
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: Have you done fairly well in other classes? How have your grades been prior to this test in that class?
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: Honestly it's just kind of all over the place. I am surviving in other classes, but with all this online stuff with the pandemic I barely learn anything. I'm basically faking it til I make it. Which I hate. But I can't learn in these conditions.
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: I hate that you feel that way about yourself, but I can also relate to having a rough time learning via online classes. I'm the same way. However, that does not disable you from being able to learn. It impedes your quality of learning, no doubt. But it isn't something that YOU can help.
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: By having an attitude of being unable to learn, you automatically lower your expectations for the success you would potentially have otherwise...

dialog.text: Yeah that's true, I just think it's not my learning style so it's a lot harder for me. I thought about waiting until things are normal enough to physically be able to go back to class before I try and finish my bachelors, but who knows when that will be
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: OMGoodness no kidding. This whole pandemic has the world in a tizzy!
dialog.speaker: supporter

dialog.text: YeahhhHonestly just talking to someone and letting it out was kinda nicemade me feel ebtter
dialog.speaker: seeker

dialog.text: If I were you I would not wait! It may not be the best option for your learning style, and it will certainly prove a greater challenge. However, taking on that challenge will bring on SWEETER rewards when you succeed! Adopt a "Can-Do" state of mind and grab the bull by the horns!
dialog.speaker: supporter
